claims.text: A nanostructured CrN-based ceramic coating on CoCrFeNi will provide low friction and low wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy is conventionally melted and cast with a typical polycrystalline microstructure.
The proposed intervention is a nanostructured CrN coating a few micrometres thick deposited by physical vapor deposition.
Coating integrity and microstructure will mediate the tribological response.
An adherent, lubricious tribolayer will form in situ at the sliding interface.
The CrN coating will act as a diffusion barrier that mitigates high-temperature oxidation of the CoCrFeNi substrate.
The ceramic coating will retain sufficient integrity to provide a mechanically robust, low-shear sliding interface.
Sliding will cause the coating to evolve gradually into a stable tribolayer.
The stable tribolayer will maintain low interfacial shear strength across the full temperature range.
Low interfacial shear strength will reduce friction and wear.
CrN-coated CoCrFeNi will have a lower coefficient of friction than uncoated CoCrFeNi from room temperature through 800 °C.
CrN-coated CoCrFeNi will have lower wear rates than uncoated CoCrFeNi from room temperature through 800 °C.
The predicted improvement depends on the high-temperature stability and self-adaptive tribolayer formation of the CrN coating.
The proposed operating boundary is sliding in ambient air from room temperature to 800 °C under approximately 10 N normal load.
The coating's microstructural evolution near 800 °C may affect tribolayer stability.
The magnitude of friction and wear reduction may vary with coating deposition parameters.
The proposed falsification tests compare coated specimens with an uncoated CoCrFeNi control at room temperature, 400 °C, and 800 °C under approximately 10 N for one hour.
Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in both friction and wear at every tested temperature, or catastrophic coating degradation, will falsify the hypothesis.
